judge_comment: The brief marks everything VERIFIED and says PROCEED, but docs/api.md says the alerts endpoint is NOT IMPLEMENTED with a non-final contract, and no sensor details screen exists (SensorListScreen is a list), so these are unsupported claims; open items are left empty, there is no mock or provisional labeling, and the sections are out of order.

The brief covers the right task and files, but its findings are padded with mislabeled VERIFIED claims (for example 'developer said' just repeating file names, and Redux 'verified' from the README). It also contradicts itself on reuse: Section H says keep it local, while decisions say reusable and shared. It lists 'Open items: none' while the prompt lists open items (filter fields unknown). Sections are out of order (H and J before F and G), and the DataTable stub (no filtering props, rows any[]) is not noted.
The BRIEF section is empty, so there is nothing to evaluate against the task or project files, and every criterion gets the minimum score.

The brief marks the alerts endpoint contract as VERIFIED and 'implemented in apiClient.ts', but docs/api.md says it is NOT IMPLEMENTED YET with a non-final contract and apiClient.ts has no alerts call. It also claims the details screen and its tabs live in SensorListScreen.tsx, which has no tabs, and it says 'no mocks are used' and 'no specific risk' despite the missing backend. It does stay within scope and reuses existing files, but its key facts are wrong and its labeling is misleading, with sections out of order (I before H, J before G).

The brief targets the right task and keeps scope tight, but it contradicts itself (PROCEED vs PROCEED WITH CONFIRMATION), marks every finding VERIFIED even though the findings only list file locations and the brief says contents were not read, leaves the test framework UNKNOWN although package.json shows jest, ignores that the files are already provided, and is truncated mid-sentence in section G with sections out of order.

The brief targets the right file and task, but it contradicts itself: it opens with PROCEED and marks every finding VERIFIED, yet says the files were not read and the retry parameters are UNKNOWN. It treats the decisions as accepted by the developer without evidence, it lists no open items or risks, and the sections are out of order.
The brief section is empty, so it covers none of sections A-G and flags none of the unknowns, such as the unimplemented alerts endpoint or the missing sensor details screen.

The brief marks findings VERIFIED on the basis of file lists that merely echo the 'developer said' text. It picks server-side filtering even though docs/api.md shows GET /sensors has no filter parameters. It says 'Decision: PROCEED' and 'Existing filter pattern VERIFIED' when none exists. It also contradicts itself by choosing a shared component while stating the feature is local. Sections A, D, F and G are missing, and the open items list says 'none'.

The brief marks everything VERIFIED although the 'findings' are just file lists echoed back (retry criteria and parameters are not in any file), proposes a non-existent src/config/retry.ts as an accepted decision, and leaves sections A, D, F and G as UNKNOWN, so the implementing AI gets no usable plan, tests or prompt.
